name: architecture-aoa-test-suite
known_facts: Analysis of Alternatives compares multiple solutions against weighted criteria
Every score needs a written justification
Do nothing is always a valid alternative
Top two alternatives within 10% is a tie with different risk profiles
Federal work needs FEAF, TOGAF, or DoDAF alignment

input.aoa_title: Identity and Access Management Platform Modernization
input.stakeholders: CISO, VP Engineering, Director of Product, Federal Compliance Officer
input.problem_statement: Legacy IAM system cannot meet FedRAMP High requirements for the new federal contract
input.constraints: Budget $2M, timeline 6 months, must achieve FedRAMP High, no customer-facing downtime
input.assumption_1: Current identity data can be extracted and transformed
input.assumption_2: Vendor APIs support our SCIM provisioning requirements
input.assumption_3: The JIT/PAG team can support a parallel-run migration
input.alt_1_description: Azure AD B2C with custom identity experience framework and custom policies
input.alt_1_kad: Microsoft ecosystem for FedRAMP High with CIAM capabilities
input.alt_2_description: Okta tenant with FedRAMP High authorization and lifecycle management
input.alt_2_kad: Best-in-class lifecycle management with broad federated protocol support
input.alt_3_description: Open-source Keycloak deployed on EKS Fargate with RDS PostgreSQL
input.alt_3_kad: Maximum control, no vendor lock-in, requires in-house expertise
input.rationale_cost: Budget is fixed at $2M, overruns would require descoping other initiatives
input.rationale_risk: Federal compliance failure means losing the contract, highest priority
input.rationale_speed: Timeline is aggressive but achievable with right vendor selection
input.rationale_maintain: Platform will operate for minimum 5 years, maintainability matters
input.rationale_security: FedRAMP High is non-negotiable, must be built in from day one
input.rationale_scale: 200K internal identities, growth is predictable and linear
input.tradeoff_1_vs_2: Azure provides deeper FedRAMP integration at lower cost; Okta offers superior identity lifecycle management
input.impact_1_vs_2: Azure approach may require Microsoft-only future; Okta lock-in is per-seat pricing risk at scale
input.tradeoff_1_vs_3: Azure offers managed service with compliance built in; Keycloak gives full control but shifts operational burden to the team
input.impact_1_vs_3: Azure failure mode is vendor dependency; Keycloak failure mode is insufficient SRE capacity for self-managed infrastructure
input.tradeoff_2_vs_3: Okta provides fastest time to FedRAMP authorization; Keycloak avoids per-seat costs but requires significant in-house expertise
input.impact_2_vs_3: Okta failure is cost overrun at scale; Keycloak failure is security misconfiguration by the operations team
input.sensitivity_change_1: If identity data transformation takes longer than 3 months, the 6-month timeline is at risk
input.sensitivity_impact_1: Okta becomes the recommended alternative due to fastest deployment timeline
input.sensitivity_change_2: If JAB backlog extends beyond 4 months, any FedRAMP In-Process vendor introduces timeline risk
input.sensitivity_impact_2: Keycloak on FedRAMP High infrastructure (GovCloud) may be faster without vendor authorization dependency
input.recommendation_rationale: Azure AD B2C scores highest overall with the best balance of FedRAMP compliance and cost, and deep integration with the existing Microsoft tenant
input.implementation_consideration_1: Parallel-run migration with identity synchronization for 30 days minimum
input.implementation_consideration_2: Custom policy development requires specialized Azure AD B2C expertise -- engage Microsoft FastTrack
input.fallback_plan: If FedRAMP High authorization timeline slips beyond 6 months, pivot to Okta which has existing FedRAMP authorization and faster deployment
input.open_item_1: Confirm FedRAMP JAB current processing timeline for Azure AD B2C
input.open_item_2: Vendor security assessment for Azure AD B2C custom policy consultant
